# Lean step 2: one fresh week, one draw a system — result (D487, D488), 2026-11-14

**Answer: by the rule written before reading, the difference is not clear.** Production covers two more of the five big matters both reader
families listed (4 against 2), which meets the rule's first half; its share of last judgements both families call supported is lower by 19
points (10 of 15 against 6 of 7), more than the one in ten the second half allows. Each half has one named cause. The first is one rule: the
three matters the clean path lacks are the company's own revenue and margin, which its request forbids as questions (D382). The second rests
mostly on one reader family: Codex failed 2 of the 4 judgements a separate reader had confirmed as supported, both of them production's;
both families call only one judgement unsupported, production's data-center revenue.

Material: 2026-09-22..28, 235 articles (232 never sent by any run), each system one draw from an empty library: the clean path
`poc/data/clean-lean-week-2026-11-14/week-r2/c1` (after D488), production `…/week/p1`. Readers: Codex (read-only) and Claude subagents, blind
to the systems and to each other; the keys are outside the repository. Model cost of the step (the one-day slice, production's draw, the
clean draw and its two stopped attempts): $4.69. One draw each: every count below is one draw.

## What each system holds at the week's end (counted from the stored runs)

| | clean c1 | production p1 |
|---|---|---|
| questions opened | 7 | 15 |
| statements written | 569, from 182 articles | 673, from 186 articles |
| thrown away for having no question | 0 | 278 |
| kept (after joining repeats) | 569 (314) | 385 |
| kept with no question: no judgement reads them | 389 | 0 |
| links to questions | 196 | 449 (126 on FY2027 total revenue, 94 on data-center revenue) |
| judgements | 37 | 72 |

## A. Big questions (40 sampled articles; eight matters, five listed by both families)

| matter | listed by | clean c1 | production p1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| M01 FY2027 revenue (total or data center) | both | **missed** | opened (v2, v4) |
| M02 FY2028 revenue | both | **missed** | opened (v3, v5) |
| M03 FY2028 gross margin against the 72%–73% outlook | both | **missed** | opened (v10) |
| M04 supply and capacity purchase commitments ($279B at Q2) | both | opened (clean-2) | **missed** |
| M05 Beijing's approval of RTX Pro 5500 purchases | both | opened (clean-7) | opened (v14, v15) |
| M06 FY2027 gross margin | one | missed | missed |
| M07 Vera Rubin revenue shipments in Q3 | one | opened (Claude) / a later deadline that does not settle Q3 (Codex) | the same split |
| M08 AMD's 2027 data-center revenue | one | missed | missed |

The families give the same status on 14 of 16 cells and on all ten cells of M01–M05. **Covered, of the five: clean 2, production 4.**

Each opened question, read beside the article it was opened from:

| | clean c1 (7) | production p1 (15) |
|---|---|---|
| worth holding | 6 (both families) | 9 (Codex) / 8 (Claude) |
| trivia | 1: the Hugging Face purchase closing | 3: "tech companies' AI spending" (nothing settles it), the Hugging Face price as a commitment, the Anthropic IPO stake |
| duplicate of another of its own | 0 | 3 by both: FY2028 growth of FY2028 revenue, Rubin by end-2027 of Rubin by January 2027, the second RTX Pro 5500 question; Claude adds data-center revenue of total revenue |

Checked by Claude against the stored runs:
- Production has no supply-commitments question: its one kept statement on the $279 billion is linked to the credit-support question (v1).
- The clean path's three misses are its rule at work. On each article where production opened v2, v3, v4, v5 and v10, the clean draw's
  stored reasoning names the request's sentence "Do not open a thesis about … a financial measure's level, growth, margin or guidance for
  any period, on its own", opens nothing and keeps the statements; 109 of 235 steps' reasoning names that sentence. The request sends such
  figures to "an open thesis about its revenue or earnings path", which nothing in an empty library is: 145 kept statements of the company's
  own figures (from 67 articles) have no question, among them the 70% growth outlook for fiscal 2028, which the articles set against the 45%
  the Street had modelled (14 statements, 14 articles), and gross-margin figures of 71% to 73% (11 statements, 9 articles).
- Both families call the Hugging Face purchase small (both systems opened a question on it). It is listed as the readers gave it; D389's
  size line is for unsigned obligations in its own test and does not rule on this question (council round 11).

## B. Judgement support (26 items: 22 real last judgements, 4 planted from earlier judgements)

| | Codex | Claude |
|---|---|---|
| planted wrong judgements caught | 4 of 4 | 4 of 4 |
| supported controls passed (confirmed first by a separate reader) | **2 of 4** | 4 of 4 |
| clean c1 (7): supported / unsupported / insufficient | 6 / 1 / 0 | 7 / 0 / 0 |
| production p1 (15) | 10 / 2 / 3 | 14 / 1 / 0 |

Supported by both families: **clean 6 of 7 (86%), production 10 of 15 (67%)**. Unsupported by both: one, production's data-center revenue (v4):
its rung is reached by a fourth-quarter growth of about 25% that the judge itself calls an allowance; no shown piece gives the rate, and the
shown 18% lands a rung lower. Called not supported by Codex alone: the clean path's credit-support total (a cap read as the amount);
production's credit-support total and its first RTX Pro 5500 question (**both are confirmed supported controls**), the Hugging Face amount and
the Anthropic stake (both also called trivia in A). Cited statements with a field error: one in each system (a quarter mislabelled; "more than
doubling to $115 billion" written as "will exceed").

## The rule, applied as written (LEAN-LOG §2)

- First half (A): production covers two more of the matters both families listed. Met by production.
- Second half (B): its share of judgements both families call supported is lower by 19 points, more than one in ten. Not met.
- **Verdict: not clear. The next small step targets the largest difference observed, not a choice of system.**

What weakens each half: A's three-matter gap is one sentence of the clean request, a product rule (D382), not a capability. B compares 7
judgements with 15, so one judgement is 14 points for the clean path; the gap comes from one family, which parted from the separate reader on two of the four supported controls, both production items, with
reasons that stand as a disagreement (a guarantee cap read as the amount; permission for two named firms read from "some firms"). As a
sensitivity note only: with those two counted as the separate reader read them, production would stand at 12 of 15; the rule's count stays
10 of 15. B at this size cannot say which system judges better.

## The largest difference observed

How each system treats the company's own revenue and margin: three of the five matters, 145 kept statements no judgement reads on one side;
on the other, the same matters opened, with two or three duplicates among them and 126 statements piled on one question.

## The source check the council asked for ($0, council round 11): do the articles hold a dispute, or only a number?

Claude's first candidate for a next step was a narrow door on the clean path: open a revenue or margin question only when the item holds both
the company's own outlook and a stated market expectation for the same measure and period. Read against every article the readers listed
for M01–M03 and every article production opened its five such questions from:

| matter | articles | hold such a pair | what they hold instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| M01 FY2027 revenue | 7 | **0** | the consensus alone ($406 billion, $412 billion, "about 90% growth"), or the company's guide for one quarter ($108 billion); the company gives no outlook for the year |
| M02 FY2028 revenue | 8 | 2 with figures (70% guided "against the 45% the Street had modelled", a gap already closed: the consensus is now about $672 billion), 1 in words | the 70% outlook alone (5 articles) |
| M03 FY2028 gross margin | 2 | 1 (the 72%–73% outlook, "analysts assume margins hold roughly steady", memory prices above what management expected) | the outlook alone |

# The small comparison D559 puts to Alex: the week of 10-06's opening articles read from a kept library and from empty (not started), 2026-11-15

**Status: prepared and proved at $0; nothing is sent without Alex's word.** Decision D559; council
`../reflection-3/cold-codex-4.md` (the test and its five proofs) and `cold-codex-5.md` (consensus).

## What it asks

Every clean measurement examined so far starts from an empty library. In the week of 10-06 that produced 13 topics, 12 of
them (by both reader families) on matters that already existed, some of which the same system had opened two weeks earlier
in its own run of the week of 09-22. The record of 2026-11-05 asks for a test that starts from a library built from real
material available before the test. This comparison is the smallest form of it: does the unchanged first step, shown the
library it built itself in the week of 09-22, stop re-creating the questions that library holds, without losing the
article's facts or the questions that are really new?

## What is sent

- The unchanged first step (`clean-arch/step1/run_live.py`; DeepSeek flash, high effort, the frozen request).
- The 11 distinct articles from which the stored October run opened its 13 topics (`inputs/articles.json`; selected because
  they opened topics: this is not a sample of the week's news).
- Each article is read twice, each read its own one-article run from a fixed starting library: `empty`
  (`inputs/initial-empty.json`) and `carried` (`inputs/initial-carried.json`: the seven topics of the September run's completed
  state). 22 reads, one draw, two at a time, on one new ledger with a ceiling of $1.00. Driver: `run_probe.py`.
- Size: the $0 dry run charged $0.46 for the 22 reads at the stored answers' sizes (the ledger's prices); the stored run needed
  14 calls for these 11 articles (three resends), so about $0.5 is expected. An estimate, not a measurement.

Frozen inputs:
- `inputs/articles.json`: sha256 `6ead553882e3c430…`
- `inputs/initial-carried.json`: sha256 `6e0669faac176a63…`
- `inputs/initial-empty.json`: sha256 `37517e5f3dc66819…`
- `inputs/manifest-base.json`: sha256 `3038c186e9a05d59…`
- `inputs/settings.json`: sha256 `7716a85da8750830…`

## Proved at $0 (`proofs/`)

| Proof | What it shows | Judged | Mutant that must fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `carried_library_proof.py` E1 | the carried library is the September run's completed state: started from empty, every article complete, the state after the last one, equal to that run's seven topics, window ending 2026-09-28 | 235 articles, 7 topics | a dropped topic: fails |
| E2 | the articles are the opening articles of the October week's 13 topics, in reading order, each equal to its stored case | 13 topics, 11 articles | a swapped article: fails |
| E3 | the real run loop, given an article's stored library, rebuilds the stored request byte for byte and the same library after | 11 of 11 | |
| E4 | an empty-start request equals a stored one as built | 1 | |
| E5 | the carried request differs from the empty one only in the open questions shown, which are the September state's | 11 of 11 pairs | |
| E6 | the same settings and system text in both stored runs and today | 2 runs | |
| `probe_dry_run_proof.py` D1 to D3 | the real driver and launcher under the trap (canned answers, placeholder keys): 22 reads, 22 sends each under a live reservation; requests stored with the intended open questions; the bytes sent from empty for the article production itself read from empty equal the bytes production sent; ledger 22 attempts, none refused, nothing left reserved | 22 reads | |
| D4 | with a ceiling below one reservation the first read is refused, the ledger stops, the probe stops, no send | 1 run | a driver that ignores the stop: fails |

Not proved by these: anything about what the model will answer. The dry run's answers were written for another library and
are not results.

## The cases, labelled before any answer (against the carried library alone)

From the two reader families' coverage answers (`../reflection-3/codex-coverage.jsonl`, `claude-coverage.jsonl`: the September
topics they named for each October topic) and my own read stored before theirs.

| October topic (stored run) | Article (sequence) | Against the carried library |
|---|---|---|
| clean-2 supply commitments | 9 | same question (September clean-2), both families |
| clean-5 the Hugging Face acquisition | 30 | same question (September clean-6), both |
| clean-7 Rubin's ramp | 76 | same question (September clean-4), both; the deadline is worded differently |
| clean-4 capital spending 2026 and 2027 | 15 | 2026 is September clean-5 (both); 2027 is not in the carried library |
| clean-1 the lease guarantee | 9 | related: September clean-1 asks the total of credit support, both |
| clean-8 the loss-share exposure | 76 | related: September clean-1, both |
| clean-6 the U.S. licence requirement | 35 | unresolved: one family names September clean-3 |
| clean-12 global AI spending | 206 | unresolved: one family names September clean-5 |
| clean-3 memory prices, clean-9 Groq's rack, clean-10 the B200 rental price, clean-11 Reflection AI, clean-13 the equity commitments | 12, 119, 173, 200, 235 | absent |

## The reading (fixed now)

Alex's rule of 2026-11-05, applied to the library actually shown: a matter the library already holds, not opened again, is
correct; a matter it lacks and that is worth a question, opened, is correct; whether the existing question received the
article's facts is checked apart.

1. Claude reads every one of the 22 answers beside its article and stores its marks first. Then two reader families apart,
   with the article, the open questions shown and the answer.
2. Per new topic in an answer: `redundant` (the library shown holds the same question), `related` (it holds the same matter
   in another shape), `new`; and whether it is worth a question by the standard's test for a big matter.
3. Per labelled case: the article's statements on that matter in each read: kept and filed under the existing question,
   kept and filed elsewhere or nowhere, or not kept. The empty read of the same article is the reference for what was there
   to keep.
4. The five absent cases are the guard against suppression: opened or not in each read.

**It supports going on** when, on the same-question cases, the carried read opens no second question on the matter and files
under the existing one at least what the empty read kept, and the absent cases open as often as in the empty read.
**It fails** when the carried read re-opens the same question in two or more of the four same-question cases; or drops the
matter's statements where the empty read kept them, in two or more; or opens two or fewer of the absent cases that the empty
read opens. Anything between is reported as it is. Ambiguous coverage stays unresolved. One draw: a reason to go on or to
stop, not an estimate of anything.

**Stopping rule of the run:** the first read the ledger refuses, that fails in transport after its retries, or whose launcher
prints no result stops the probe; an answer the step's own checks reject is that read's outcome.

# Does one missing fact change one stored judgement? Result of the six-call test (D510, under D439), 2026-11-15

Design: `EFFECT-TEST-DESIGN.md` (version 2, frozen before the send). Script: `effect_test.py`. Raw replies, answers and spend:
`poc/data/clean-effect-test-2026-11-15/v7-e379/`. Blind rankings: `codex-stance.jsonl`, `claude-stance.jsonl`. Tally:
`tally_effect.py`, `tally-effect.txt`.

## The outcome, by the rule written before the send: inconclusive

- Six calls, six HTTP attempts, all six answers valid (the judge's schema and its own check against the request sent). **$0.0093** at
  the published rates (ceiling $0.25). Spend recorded under D439: about $18.4 before, about $18.41 after.
- **The answer did not move:** all three controls and all three answers with the fact are answer 1 (yes).
- **The rankings did not separate:** in both blind readers' rankings the conditions overlap: the firmest is a control, the least
  firm is a control, and the answers with the fact lie between (one reader ties a control and an answer with the fact). The controls
  alone span the whole range, so the control's own variation is as large as anything between the conditions. The readers were not
  told the conditions, but the packet showed each answer's cited ids, e379 among them for two answers: the result is that the
  rankings did not separate, not that the conditions could not be told apart.
- By the design this is inconclusive: it does not show the gap is without effect. One request, three sends a condition.

## Every answer

| Answer | Rung | Cites e379 | Marks e379 as pushing | Codex rank | Claude rank | Its words on doubt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| control 3 | 1 | - | - | 1 | 1 | "a possible cap or staged approval, but the thesis requires approval of a purchase" |
| with the fact 1 | 1 | no | toward the last answer | 2 | 2 | "These reports are unverified and repeated coverage ... is not independent confirmation" |
| with the fact 3 | 1 | yes | toward the last answer | 3 | 3 | "The reported shipment plan and domestic-policy constraints temper confidence" |
| control 2 | 1 | - | - | 4 | 4 | "Domestic-chip preferences, possible bundling, and the H200 precedent temper the forecast" |
| with the fact 2 | 1 | yes | toward the last answer | 4 | 5 | "Domestic substitution, possible bundling, and the H200 precedent temper confidence" |
| control 1 | 1 | - | - | 6 | 6 | "The reporting is unconfirmed ... U.S. export uncertainty, domestic-silicon preferences, possible bundling, and the H200 precedent" |

## What Claude read in the six answers and the two requests (every trace)

- **The judge registered the added statement and did not weigh it in words.** In all three answers with the fact, its list of how
  each statement pushes marks e379 "toward the last answer" (against "yes"); two of the three cite it. None of the three names the
  RTX Pro 6000D or a September 2025 stop order in its reasons.
- **The request already held a precedent of a like kind.** Under this question the judge was already shown that Chinese regulators
  mostly blocked imports of Nvidia's H200 after Washington had approved them (e566), and that H200 use was restricted. The stored
  answer and two of the three controls already temper "yes" with "the H200 precedent". This is a reason the test may not have been
  able to show an effect; it is not proof that the added stop order added nothing.
- All six answers rest "yes" on one reported signal (MIIT told firms it intends to approve) and on the question needing only one
  approved purchase by the deadline; each says no formal decision against is reported.

## A fault in the reading, found after the send

The blind readers' second mark, `uses_precedent`, was worded as "an earlier Chinese order telling firms to stop buying a related
Nvidia chip". The H200 blocking already in the request fits those words, so the readers marked "yes" for two controls and one answer
with the fact, all of which name the H200 and none the RTX Pro 6000D. The mark could not tell the added fact from what the request
already had. It decides nothing here (the rankings do not separate), but it was written without first checking what the stored
request and the stored answer already said on the point; the stored answer's "the H200 precedent" was on screen before the send.

## What this result may and may not be said to show

- Shown: for this one request, adding the missing statement did not move the answer in three sends, and two blind rankings of
  firmness did not separate the conditions; the judge's structured output marked the statement as pushing against "yes" in all
  three, an observed change in what it wrote, not in what it chose.
- Not shown: that the delivery gap of D506 and D508 is without effect on judgements (one case, three sends; this case's request
  already carried a like precedent); a rate; anything about which system carries forward.

## Council (thread mx, round 23, under D439; `clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/council/mx-challenge-22.md`, `mx-codex-23.md`): consensus

- The council checked all six raw replies against the recorded answers and re-ran the schema and the judge's check: all match and
  pass. The outcome is inconclusive.
- The omission is real as delivery (kept, absent from the question's requests, judged relevant by both census readers) and the
  judge's marks on it are an observed change in its structured output; no change of answer and no separated change of confidence
  was established.
- The other confirmed cases are not shown to be weaker, and a fix is not shown to be a patch: neither can be said without a
  mechanism and its share. What is supported is "do not build on this evidence now".
- **Decided under D439 (D511):** no further send and no change on this delivery line now; the confirmed omissions, the 23 open pairs
  and this inconclusive test stay open evidence; the decision D507 left for after the sizing ("then decide whether to change") is
  taken as: defer. The next step is a cold reflection council over the whole record, which ranks the remaining losses from the
  product goal and proposes one next test with its falsifier.

## Lessons

1. **Read the control for facts of the same kind before writing the measure.** The stored answer's "the H200 precedent" was on
   screen before the send, and the reader's mark was still worded so that it fits.
2. **A reader's "bears" is not a judge's changed answer.** The census counts the first; only a send shows the second.
3. **The judge's structured marks moved while its answer and reasons did not.** They are a cheaper and more sensitive observable
   than a reading of reasons, and belong in the outcomes written before a send, with what they can and cannot show.
4. **Stepping back is a decision.** After several results that separated nothing, the next step is chosen from the goal by the
   council, not from the last result.

# How large is the gap? Result of the census over everything the new system kept in the fresh week (D507), 2026-11-15

Design: `CLASS-CENSUS-DESIGN.md` (version 2, frozen before any reader). First readers: `codex-class-part1..6.jsonl`,
`claude-class-part1..6.jsonl`. Candidates and the instrument's check: `class_candidates.py`, `candidates-first.txt`,
`class-candidates.json`. The fresh pair: `*-class-settle-*.jsonl`. Tally: `tally_class.py`, `tally-class.txt`; the one hand merge:
`class-merges.json`. The run: the new system's stored fresh-week draw of D489 (567 kept statements, seven questions, 37 judgements).
Cost: $0; nothing was sent to a model and nothing changed in the system.

## The size, as this reading found it

| | |
|---|---|
| kept statements read against the seven questions (each by both families, all seven questions marked) | 567 |
| links the system made (a judge is shown exactly these) | 196 |
| candidates: listed for a question by a first reader and not linked to it | 63 (17 by both families, 16 Codex only, 30 Claude only) |
| **confirmed missing** (both fresh readers, shown everything the judge had and the article: in the article, not shown, bears) | **5 statements: 3 fact-and-question pairs, in 3 of the 7 questions** |
| open (the fresh readers differ) | 23 candidate statement-and-question pairs (not 23 distinct facts: some repeat one fact) |
| dropped (both: does not bear, or both: already shown) | 35 |

**The confirmed count is a minimum found by this reading, not a complete census, and one week of seven questions gives no general
rate.** A fact neither first reader listed is not found. The 23 open pairs are uncertainty, not an upper bound on what is missing.
Links and missing facts are different units: three beside 196 does not show the gap to be small.

## The three confirmed missing facts (each read by hand in the stored request)

1. **Supply commitments (v2; its last answer: the top band, $200 billion or more).** The CEO said NVIDIA would double the number of
   chips it sells next year (2027): three statements from three articles, one fact (the merge and its reason are in
   `class-merges.json`). Two were linked to no question, one to the Vera Rubin question. The request holds the CFO's 70% outlook and a
   conditional "could double if supply allowed", not this forecast. The readers: twice the chips needs more secured supply; the top
   band more likely to hold. Chip sales are not a figure for purchase commitments: the bearing is by a step of reasoning.
2. **Approval of Blackwell sales to China (v3; its last answer: still open).** "Washington has not said whether the card may be shipped
   to China at all": that the RTX Pro 5500's exemption is industry executives' reading, not a U.S. position. Linked to the RTX Pro
   5500 question only. The request holds the executives' expectation, not Washington's silence. The readers: the U.S. half is
   unsettled even for this chip; "yes" less likely. The statement is about the RTX Pro 5500 and the question about Blackwell sales
   more broadly: its bearing is an inference, not a ruling on Blackwell exports.
3. **MIIT's approval of RTX Pro 5500 purchases (v7; its last answer: yes).** "In September 2025, Beijing told firms to stop buying
   Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000D." Read at article 163, six articles before this question opened at 169, and linked to the export question.
   The request holds no earlier stop order. The readers: a precedent on a sibling chip from the same authority; "yes" less certain.
   **This one bears against the answer the judgement gave.**

By kind: two were linked to another question while the question they also bear on was open; one was read before its question
existed and was already linked to another question, so the later-linking step did not reconsider it (see the correction below).

## The open band (23)

- 13: one fresh reader says the fact bears and the other that it does not (the per-gigawatt figures and a per-gigawatt cost estimate
  under the credit-support question; Micron's capacity and memory tightness under supply commitments; Huawei's and Alibaba's chips, a
  scholar's view of China's chip shortage, a state dinner and a spokesperson's remark under the RTX Pro 5500 question; two others).
- 10: they differ on whether the judge already had it. Five of these are the 70% growth outlook repeated by other outlets, which the
  supply-commitments request does state (read by hand in D506): delivered in substance, though left open by the rule.
- The two families' bars differ throughout: of the 63 candidates, the fresh Codex reader marked 53 as bearing and the fresh Claude
  reader 34. Where "an analyst reasons onward" stops is not settled by these readers.

## The earlier finding did not hold with a second pair

D506's finding (the per-gigawatt revenue opportunity under the credit-support question) stands under D506's rule: four readers
confirmed it there. Under this census's rule it is an open lead: the first readers listed it again (one statement by both families,
one by Claude) and a new fresh pair split. One says it sizes the supported capacity; the other that a product's revenue per gigawatt
is not a credit-support amount and that the top answer already holds, a reason that sets aside the design's own test (a fact that
changes how likely an answer is counts). Both results are on record. The split is a reading problem, not two settled standards.

## The instrument's own check

- Of the 196 links the system made, the first readers also list: Codex 126 (64%), Claude 108 (55%). About four in ten of the
  statements the system files under a question are not answer-bearing for a reader family: the system files more widely than these
  readers would. This census did not examine whether such statements belong there.
- Who listed the candidates first: of the 17 both families listed, 1 is confirmed, 4 open, 12 dropped; of 30 Claude only, 3
  confirmed, 13 open, 14 dropped; of 16 Codex only, 1 confirmed, 6 open, 9 dropped.
- One reader session printed the folder's file names on entering it (names only; it reports opening nothing else).

## What this result may and may not be said to show

- Shown, for one stored week and draw: at least three kept facts that both fresh readers say bear on a question never reached its
  judge, in three of seven questions; one of them bears against the judgement's answer; twenty-three more candidates are undecided
  between two reader bars.
- Not shown: that any judgement would have changed (not measured); a rate for the system in general; that the gap is isolated (a
  low confirmed count is a minimum); anything about production or about which system carries forward.

## Council (thread mx, round 21; `clean-arch/step1-unfiled-2026-11-08/council/mx-challenge-20.md`, `mx-codex-21.md`): consensus, with corrections

- Stated as: three confirmed fact-and-question pairs in three questions, from five statements; 23 unresolved candidate pairs; a
  minimum. Corrected in this page: the 23 are pairs, not distinct facts; "small beside 196 links" compared different units and is
  removed; the D506 finding is not disproved, both results stand; the bearing of two of the three facts is by inference and is said
  so.
- The families' split is not handed to Alex as a ruler to set: one fresh reader's reason ("the top answer already holds") departs
  from the written test.
- **The one test to offer, his to open (it sends):** the effect on the judgement, on the strongest case only. The RTX Pro 5500
  question answered "yes" without the earlier report that Beijing had told firms to stop buying the related RTX Pro 6000D. The
  stored last request of that question re-sent as stored and re-sent with that one stored statement added in the judge's own
  format (its id, source, date and quote), three sends each on the same day: six judge calls, about one cent at the published rates
  (the stored call: 5,628 tokens in, 2,514 out), ceiling $0.25. The control is rebuilt byte for byte first; what counts as a
  meaningful loss of confidence in "yes" is written before the send (citing the new fact is not enough); all six answers are read
  blind to their condition. A difference inside the control's own variation, or none, is inconclusive, not proof of no effect; a
  directional difference in three sends is a bounded signal on this request, not the size of the effect on the product.

## Lessons

1. **Count in one unit.** The draft set three facts beside 196 links and 23 pairs beside them as if they measured one thing.
2. **A finding is the output of its rule and its readers.** The same fact was confirmed by four readers under one rule and split by
   two under the next; neither erases the other, and a result that rests on two fresh readers says so.
3. **Check a reader's reason against the written test.** One fresh reader dropped facts because the answer was already on its top
   band, though the brief counts a change in likelihood; a mark given for a reason outside the test is noted as such.
4. **After a census, test the effect where the product is judged, on the strongest case first.** Six calls on the one fact that
   opposes a stored answer decide more than a wider reading of all 23.

## Correction (2026-11-15, found by the reflection council "my", round 3, and checked in the stored run)

This page said that nothing in the new system files an earlier statement under a question opened later, and that a judge is shown
the statements linked "when their articles were read". Both are wrong as written. **The new system has a later-linking step**
(`clean-arch/step3/library.py`, `link_later`): when a question opens, the system checks the earlier groups of statements (a
statement with its repeats) **whose original statement arrived without a question** (a batch that fails twice stays pending and is
tried again; none stayed pending in this run). In this week: seven calls, 516 group-and-question checks, 2 linked (both to the Vera
Rubin question); of the 196 links, 194 were made when the statement's article was read and 2 by this step. **A group whose original
arrived under another question is excluded, even if the new question also needs it:** e379 (the group `163:e3` in the stored
library) arrived linked to the export question at article 163, so it was not among the 166 checked when the RTX Pro 5500 question
opened at article 169. The counts and findings of this page do not change; the description of the cause does: the
case is "linked elsewhere and so never reconsidered", not "nothing looks back". Production does not link an earlier record to a
question opened later (D456: none of 3,225 links in six draws points back; a later article that repeats the fact can still deliver
it; `clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/unlinked-trace/UNLINKED-TRACE-RESULT.md`, which found that in those draws, on the graded
questions of the July window, such unlinked facts cost no final answer).

# The distance to the first gate, topic by topic, over the four stored readings (D556, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

What this is: every stored reading of the step that writes answer choices, restated per topic with the collector's own rules
and reconciled to its report (`first_gate_map.py`; `proofs/first-gate-map.json`). A mark two readers agree on stands; where they
differ it takes the two third readers' ruling when they rule alike, and is "open" otherwise. Classes come from the marks, the
rulings and the reason the step gave for declining; nothing is judged anew. What it cannot do: prove the gate out of reach on
future topics, show that any change would work, or trigger D544's reversal. The four readings are four populations read in
different ways and stay apart; the 104 topics include repeated runs of the same news.

## 1. The four readings, reconciled

| Reading | Topics | Right in two of three attempts | Of them by written choices | Line (Alex's 35 and 28 of 44, scaled) | Reconciled to its report |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alex's 44 topics, fourth reading (the step was tuned on them; frozen after) | 44 | 40, or 34 with the open points against | 31, or 25 | 35 and 28 | yes, both countings |
| July, three runs over the same 14 days | 40 | 32, or 19 | 22, or 13 | 32 and 26 | yes, both countings |
| The fresh week (one Codex reader and Claude's own marks; no third reader) | 7 | 4, or 0 | 4, or 0 | 6 and 5 | no report to reconcile to; the marks are those of D545 |
| The week of 10-06 (all 13 topics; the wider count is 12) | 13 | 10, or 3 | 7, or 1 | 11 and 9 | yes, both countings |

## 2. Agreed faults on the four zero-fault lines

| Reading | Attempts | Another question (Q) | A part unlisted (L) | Ranges or rungs (R) | Unjustified refusal (N) | Together |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alex's 44 | 132 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 6 attempts on 5 topics |
| July | 120 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 7 marks on 6 attempts, 6 topics |
| The fresh week | 21 | 0 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 attempts on 3 topics |
| The week of 10-06 | 39 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 8 marks on 7 attempts, 5 topics |

No reading has a zero-fault line set clean, and the faults are not the same from one reading to the next: ranges in the two
earlier readings, unlisted parts in the two later ones, a different question or a doubtful refusal in three of four.

## 3. The topics without two right written answers, by what stands in the way

Counted with every open point for the answer. A topic can sit under more than one heading; "would be enough alone" is an
upper bound on paper: it assumes the declined or faulty attempts would otherwise have been sound, which nothing shows.

**I agree with the direction and the revised answers to Alex. The pilot needs four concrete adjustments before it is built.**

1. **Include the controls and completeness cases deliberately.** A random selection of six of seven new-system questions could omit one of the three D508 questions. Include those three first, then randomly select the other three. Include at least one independently checked supported control among the six old-system questions; otherwise the pilot cannot report whether Alex accepted a sound control. Publish the selection rule and seed before drawing. The old system’s controls include two that one reader disputed, so keep those disagreements visible after the blind reading. [Fresh-week result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:66), [D508 census]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/delivery-class/CLASS-CENSUS-RESULT.md)

2. **Show the material needed for the exact judgement being compared.** The existing support marks were made against what the judge was shown, not only its cited passages. Put the cited passages on the card and make the **complete request and sources accessible**, so Alex can assess the same question; report any mark made without inspecting the full material separately. Verify that each planted answer has the same material and answer choices it had in its original control, and that no matching real card reveals the plant. [Fresh-week result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:66)

3. **Separate relevance from changed answers on the three completeness sheets.** D508 established that two fresh readers found the facts relevant and absent; it did **not** establish that they change the answer. Ask Alex first whether each fact bears on the question, then whether it would change the answer, confidence, neither, or whether he cannot tell. Present the full judgement request and date with each sheet, and identify the independently checked negative control in the sealed key. On all other cards, completeness remains **not assessed**. [D508 result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/delivery-class/CLASS-CENSUS-RESULT.md), [D511 effect test]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/effect/EFFECT-TEST-RESULT.md)

4. **Treat the stopping signals as diagnostic, not as a calibrated pass line.** Three repeats and two wrong answers are too few to establish an error rate. Two repeat disagreements or two missed plants should trigger investigation and redesign, but even perfect marks would not prove reliability. Record the elapsed time and where it went; exceeding half an hour may mean shortening the packet or changing the unit, rather than automatically proving the unit wrong.

For the **two “no question” cards**, show the matter and source, but mark answer support **not applicable**. Keep the model families’ original marks and their scope attached to each card: their prior question-worth and support readings did not necessarily judge the same completeness sheets or planted-answer selection.

Two wording refinements for Alex:

- The week had **235 articles, 232 previously unsent**. Say “a fresh-week stored comparison,” rather than implying every article was unseen. [Week result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:8)
- Say the July end-to-end result **could not rank the systems at that size and under that matching rule**. Its spread does not prove that no end-to-end comparison could rank them. [Comparison sizing]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/comparison/COMPARISON-SIZING.md)

The pilot can be prepared from stored material without new model calls. The **$0 label excludes Alex’s time and any unpriced preparation work**.
